# Shifty Habits

> A habit tracker for shift workers. Habits attach to shift types and roster cycles rather than to fixed calendar days, so a rotating roster, a night shift crossing midnight, or a rostered day off does not break tracking the way a conventional habit app does. Android only, free, and all data stays on the device.

Shifty Habits exists because mainstream habit trackers assume a fixed Monday-to-Friday week. Shift workers do not have one. The app replaces the calendar week with the user's actual roster as the unit that habits are scheduled and scored against.

## How it differs from a conventional habit tracker

- **Habits attach to shift types, not weekdays.** A habit assigned to "Night" appears only on night shifts. An optional weekday filter can be applied on top of that.
- **Two roster models.** A repeating cycle (for example 4 days on, 4 nights on, 4 off) or a changing roster typed in month by month. The rest of the app is identical either way.
- **"Today" follows the active shift, not midnight.** A shift starting at 22:00 keeps its habits, reminders and logs on the day the shift started, even after midnight passes. Shifts of up to 72 hours are supported.
- **Streaks skip days a habit does not apply to.** A rostered day off, a non-matching shift type, or a day that has not happened yet is stepped over rather than counted as a miss.
- **Scores can be filtered to one shift type.** A habit's history and score can be narrowed to nights alone or days alone, rather than reporting one blended number.
- **Sleep Mode (Pro, Android 10+).** A Do Not Disturb mode of the app's own for sleeping after a shift: starred contacts (or whoever the user picks) and repeat callers still ring through so work can call someone in, volumes are set for sleep and restored afterwards, and it ends itself at a chosen time. Each shift type can carry a sleep window anchored to the shift (for example, eight hours starting an hour after a night ends), so Sleep Mode switches on by itself as the roster moves. The user's own Do Not Disturb settings are never changed.
- **Reminders timed to the shift or to bedtime.** A reminder can be set relative to shift start, shift end, or bedtime, which the app works out from the roster (the Sleep Mode window where one is set, otherwise from when the next shift starts). An optional End Shift button (Settings, End Shift) makes end-of-shift reminders wait until the user taps End Shift on the notification, for shifts that run over.
- **A sample preview.** A new install opens on a sample roster with months of history to look around before setting anything up; "Set up my own" leaves it, and none of the sample data carries over.
- **Day notes tagged to habits.** A note on a day can be tagged to habits with #, and tagged notes appear as markers on that habit's graph.
- **Milestone celebrations.** Streaks are celebrated at 10, 30, 100 and 365 days and consistency at 60, 70, 80 and 90 percent; a streak that is lost and rebuilt is celebrated again.
- **Per-shift suggestions.** When a habit keeps slipping on one shift type while going well on the others, its page points it out and can make a separate version of the habit for that shift.
- **Auto-complete for habits done by default.** A habit can be set so that any applicable day left unlogged is marked done once it is over, so only the misses need a tap.
- **Positive and negative habits both supported**, with a choice of whether a negative habit scores on an inverted scale or the same "higher is better" scale as everything else.

## Privacy and data handling

- No account, no sign-up, no cloud sync, no backend. The app works fully offline.
- All data is stored locally in SQLite on the device.
- The database is excluded from Android cloud backup; device-to-device transfer is allowed.
- Optional anonymous diagnostics (Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics). No habit name, shift name, note, pasted URL or linked package name is ever sent.
- In the UK, the EEA and Switzerland the app asks once on first launch and collects nothing until the user agrees; declining or dismissing leaves it off. Elsewhere diagnostics are on by default and can be turned off at any time in Settings, Privacy. Which applies is decided from the device's own time zone — the app never looks up the user's location.
- Users can export and restore their own data themselves.
- Sleep Mode needs Android's Do Not Disturb access, used only to switch its own Do Not Disturb mode and volumes. The app never reads contacts or call history; Android applies the caller rules itself.

## Availability and pricing

- Android, on Google Play, in a growing number of countries with more being added: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.shiftyhabits.app
- No iOS version.
- If it is unavailable in a given country, the developer asks to be emailed at ShiftyHabits@gmail.com with the country, which informs the rollout order.
- The app ships in twelve languages, most of them machine-translated and not yet reviewed by native speakers. Corrections are actively wanted at ShiftyHabits@gmail.com and can be made one phrase at a time.
- Free, with no limit on the number of habits. Backup and restore are free.
- An optional one-off paid upgrade (Pro) adds a longer history window, alternate scoring models, a streak-over-time overlay, more than one active roster cycle, restoring deleted habits, and Sleep Mode.
- Launch promotion: until 1 January 2027 every Pro feature is free for everyone, and anyone who opens the app before that date keeps Pro permanently, with no purchase.

## Who it is for

Nurses, paramedics, police, firefighters, mining and FIFO workers, factory and plant operators, security staff, hospitality staff, pilots and cabin crew, drivers — anyone on a rotating roster, a 24/7 shift pattern, or night work.

It works just as well for a regular 9-to-5, Monday-to-Friday job (set up as a weekly cycle of five work days and two off), and for someone who stops working shifts: they change the roster to the new pattern and keep using the app. Habit tracking and Sleep Mode are just as useful without shifts.

## Guides

Longer-form writing on the site, each answering a question shift workers actually ask. The full list of questions they cover, each linked to its answer, is on the guides page: https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/

- **How to build habits as a shift worker when your schedule keeps changing** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/habit-consistency-with-changing-shifts/
  Anchor habits to shift events (before shift, after shift, first day off) rather than clock times; give each habit a scaled-down version per shift type; measure opportunities taken rather than calendar days.
- **How to maintain a routine when working night shifts** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/night-shift-routine/
  Sleep is the primary habit on nights. Covers protecting the sleep window, bright light early in the shift and darkness on the commute home, stopping caffeine at the shift's halfway point, eating patterns, and the changeover days entering and leaving a night block.
- **Common shift rotation patterns explained** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/shift-rotation-patterns/
  4-on-4-off, 2-2-3 (Panama/Pitman), DuPont, Continental (in the UK usually 2 days, 2 nights, 4 off on 12-hour shifts; also an 8-hour 2-2-2-2 version) and Southern Swing, each drawn day by day with cycle length and shift length. All average 42 hours a week, because 168 hours of weekly cover divided between four crews is 42 hours each.
- **Why your habit streak keeps breaking, and how to stop it** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/streaks-and-days-off/
  Conventional trackers count calendar days, so a rostered day off is indistinguishable from a skipped day. Streaks should count only applicable days, treat an unlogged day still in progress as pending rather than failed, and keep an overnight shift on the date it started.
- **What to look for in a habit tracker for shift workers** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/best-habit-tracker-for-shift-workers/
  Answers whether there is a habit tracker designed for shift workers (yes: Shifty Habits) and what to look for in one: habits attached to shift types rather than weekdays, a roster model, days off not counted as misses, a day that follows the shift rather than midnight, shift-relative reminders, per-shift-type scores, and an alternative to streaks. Also covers tracking habits when every week looks different and building habits without daily streaks.
- **How to build a routine without a fixed wake-up time** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/routine-without-fixed-wake-up-time/
  Build routines around four bookends that happen every day whatever the shift — waking, before shift, after shift, before sleep — with a minimum version for hard days. Includes a morning routine for night workers, whose morning is mid-afternoon.
- **How to get back into a routine after night shift — and keep it on days off** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/back-into-routine-after-night-shift/
  After the last night shift, a short sleep, afternoon daylight, normal meal times and an ordinary bedtime; most people are close to normal by day two. Keeps a days-off minimum (wake window, one movement, one reset task) so routines don't dissolve on days off.
- **How to manage your sleep routine when working shifts** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/sleep-routine-for-shift-workers/
  Plan sleep per shift type (early, late, night, day off), make the room dark, cool and quiet for daytime sleep, and run the same short wind-down before every sleep. Most adults need at least seven hours per 24, not necessarily in one block. Covers naps, caffeine cut-off, forward rotation, and when to see a doctor.
- **How to exercise consistently when you work rotating shifts** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/exercise-on-rotating-shifts/
  Give each shift type its own exercise slot and size (after earlies, before lates, after waking on nights, long sessions on days off), set targets per roster cycle rather than per week, keep a minimum version for nights, and keep intense sessions away from the sleep window.
- **How to eat healthy when you work irregular hours** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/healthy-eating-irregular-hours/
  Plan meals by shift type, eat the main meal before a night shift and keep food between roughly midnight and 06:00 light, always bring food from home, and batch cook on the last day off.
- **Staying motivated, and making time for goals, when you work shifts** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/motivation-and-goals-on-shift-work/
  Don't rely on motivation after a shift: decide in advance and shrink habits to what you would do exhausted. Put personal goals on specific days of the roster (usually mid-break), and set goals per roster cycle rather than per week when the roster keeps changing.
- **How to keep habits going on a 4-on, 4-off roster** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/habits-on-4-on-4-off-roster/
  Treat the eight-day (or sixteen-day, if days and nights alternate) cycle as the week, keep only minimum versions of habits on 12-hour work days, give each of the four days off a job (recover, live, live, reset), and judge habits per cycle.
- **The Panama (2-2-3) shift pattern explained** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/panama-shift-pattern/
  A 14-day cycle of 12-hour shifts (2 on, 2 off, 3 on, 2 off, 2 on, 3 off): 84 hours a fortnight, 42 a week on average, repeating on the same weekdays with every other weekend off as a three-day break. Covers the 28-day version alternating day and night fortnights, and planning habits per fortnight. In Shifty Habits it is the "2 on, 2 off, 3 on" preset.
- **The continental shift pattern explained** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/continental-shift-pattern/
  In the UK, two 12-hour days, two 12-hour nights and four days off on an eight-day, four-crew cycle averaging 42 hours a week; also the 8-hour version (two mornings, two afternoons, two nights, two off). Covers sleeping on two nights at a time and habits on a cycle that drifts through the week. In Shifty Habits the 12-hour version is the "2 days, 2 nights, 4 off" preset.
- **How to make Do Not Disturb follow your shift roster** — https://shiftyhabits.com/guides/do-not-disturb-by-shift-schedule/
  Android's built-in Do Not Disturb schedules repeat by weekday, so they can't follow a rotating roster. Compares four options: turning it on by hand, a calendar-event rule (Pixel and near-stock Android; runs during events, so sleep blocks must be in the calendar; not available in Samsung's Modes and Routines), automation apps such as MacroDroid or Tasker, and Shifty Habits' Sleep Mode, which works sleep windows out from the roster itself. Recommends letting starred contacts and repeat callers through so work can still call.
